Dutch record producer [[YoungKio]] composed the instrumental and made it available for purchase online in 2018. [[File:Lil Nas X (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Lil Nas X (pictured) leased the beat for "Old Town Road" anonymously on an online store from producer YoungKio for $30.<ref name="BI"/>]]
Country rap, and its subgenre, country trap, emerged onto the mainstream following the American rapper [[Young Thug]]'s experimental mixtape ''[[Beautiful Thugger Girls]]'' (2017).<ref name="ThugSlime"/> Lil Nas X has cited Young Thug as a pioneer of country trap.<ref name="TIME">{{Cite magazine |author=Andrew R. Chow |date=March 30, 2019 |title=Lil Nas X on 'Old Town Road' and the Billboard Controversy |url=https://time.com/5561466/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard/ |access-date=March 30, 2019 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |archive-date=October 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011091057/https://time.com/5561466/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In May 2018, [[Lil Tracy]] and [[Lil Uzi Vert]] ignited the trend with their country rap single "Like a Farmer (Remix)".<ref name="ThugSlime">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-five-things-to-know-8503019/|title=5 Things to Know About 'Old Town Road' Rapper Lil Nas X|magazine=Billboard|author=Michael Saponara|date=March 22, 2019|access-date=March 29, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefader.com/2019/03/27/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard-country-chart-removal|title=Billboard erases Lil Nas X's 'Old Town Road' from country music chart|website=[[The Fader]]|author=Salvatore Maicki|date=March 27, 2019|access-date=March 29, 2019|quote=Lil Nas X's hit is one of the latest entries in a storied canon of country rap, a trend reignited last year by Lil Tracy and Lil Uzi Vert's "Like a Farmer."|archive-date=June 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626185316/https://www.thefader.com/2019/03/27/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-billboard-country-chart-removal|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2018, Lil Nas X dropped out of college to pursue a music career even though he was discouraged by his parents. He moved in with his sister, spending time promoting his music on the Internet while having just three hours of sleep each night. Lil Nas X found the beat for "Old Town Road" in October 2018 and began writing after his sister told him he had to move out soon.<ref name="Recording">{{cite tweet|number=1155911402827046913|user=LilNasX|title=🤠<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=August 27, 2019|date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> Lil Nas X felt like he was "out of options" and said that his sister's and parents' frustrations with him inspired the song's chorus, "can't nobody tell me nothing". Within a month of writing it, Lil Nas X chose to alter the song's meaning so that the "old town road" would be a symbol of success.<ref name="TIME"/> Lil Nas X recorded the song on December 2, 2018,<ref name="Recording"/> at the CinCoYo Recording Studio in [[Atlanta]],<ref>{{cite AV media notes|title=''"Old Town Road"''|others=[[Lil Nas X]]; [[Billy Ray Cyrus]]|year=2019|type=vinyl notes|publisher=[[Columbia Records]]}}</ref> and released it the same day on [[SoundCloud]] under the title "Old Town Road (I Got the Horses in the Back)".<ref name="Recording"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://slate.com/culture/2021/04/lil-nas-x-montero-call-me-by-your-name-billboard-memes.html|title="Montero" Is the Gayest No. 1 Single in Billboard History|date=April 9, 2021|first=Chris|last=Molanphy|work=[[Slate (magazine)|Slate]]|access-date=April 10, 2021|archive-date=April 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410005334/https://slate.com/culture/2021/04/lil-nas-x-montero-call-me-by-your-name-billboard-memes.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

The Dutch record producer [[YoungKio]] produced the beat a year before the song's release and uploaded it as ''Future Type Beat''<ref name="youngKio GQ"/> to his online store for selling [[Hip hop production|beats]]. He sampled [[Nine Inch Nails]]' track "[[34 Ghosts IV]]" after finding it from his YouTube algorithm's suggested videos. YoungKio downloaded the song and imported the file to [[FL Studio]], chopping up the Nine Inch Nails sample and filtering it so that it sounded like an old [[field recording]], then reordering sections in an effort to make the austere original more catchy and adding drums underneath.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://benmorss.com/rock-theory/old-town-road/|title=The long and winding "Old Town Road"|date=August 16, 2020|access-date=August 22, 2020|author=Ben Morss|archive-date=September 23, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923083410/https://benmorss.com/rock-theory/old-town-road/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="youngKio GQ">{{cite web | last=Cea | first=Max | title=The Producer of "Old Town Road" Is 19, Dutch, and Living His Dreams | website=GQ | date=April 23, 2019 | url=https://www.gq.com/story/youngkio-old-town-road-interview | access-date=August 16, 2023 | archive-date=April 11, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210411185724/https://www.gq.com/story/youngkio-old-town-road-interview | url-status=live }}</ref> He had never heard of Nine Inch Nails before stumbling upon "34 Ghosts IV".<ref name="BI">{{Cite web|work=Business Insider|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-nine-inch-nails-sample-2019-5|title=Lil Nas X's country-trap hit 'Old Town Road' samples a Nine Inch Nails song — and the band might have a claim to some of the royalties|date=May 31, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019|author=Pamela Engel|archive-date=June 25, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190625023032/https://www.businessinsider.com/lil-nas-x-old-town-road-nine-inch-nails-sample-2019-5|url-status=live}}</ref> YoungKio did not have the intention of the beat being country related and did not see it as a country music instrumental.<ref name="YoungKio">{{cite magazine | last=Lamarre | first=Carl | title='Old Town Road' Producer YoungKio on How Lil Nas X's Song Came to Life | magazine=Billboard | date=March 28, 2019 | url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/old-town-road-producer-youngkio-interview-lil-nas-x-8504409/ | access-date=August 16, 2023 | archive-date=May 6, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230506070402/https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/old-town-road-producer-youngkio-interview-lil-nas-x-8504409/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Lil Nas X bought the beat from YoungKio for $30,<ref name="BI"/> but since purchases on his online store were anonymous, YoungKio did not know the song was purchased by Lil Nas X until he saw it in an [[Instagram]] meme in December 2018.<ref name="YoungKio"/> Nine Inch Nails founder [[Trent Reznor]] later said that, shortly after the song began gaining traction, he received a call from Lil Nas X's manager about the sample, asking for clearance to use it, which he granted. He described the song as "undeniably hooky".<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Grow |first=Kory |title=Trent Reznor Breaks Silence on 'Undeniably Hooky' 'Old Town Road' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/trent-reznor-old-town-road-903889/ |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]  |date=October 25, 2019 |access-date=November 19, 2019|archive-url=https://archive.today/20240828181919/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/trent-reznor-old-town-road-903889/|archive-date=August 28, 2024}}</ref>

On December 4, 2018, a day after the original version's release, Lil Nas X tweeted that he wanted [[Billy Ray Cyrus]] on the song.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1070125203345342464|user=LilNasX|title=twitter please help me get billy ray cyrus on this<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=April 5, 2019|date=December 4, 2018}}</ref> Lil Nas X knew of Cyrus because of his role on the Disney Channel television series ''[[Hannah Montana]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/billy-ray-cyrus-interview-hannah-montana-old-town-road-2020-1|title=Billy Ray Cyrus says Lil Nas X only knew he made country music because of 'Hannah Montana'|website=[[Business Insider]]|access-date=February 1, 2020|archive-date=February 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201212930/https://www.businessinsider.com/billy-ray-cyrus-interview-hannah-montana-old-town-road-2020-1|url-status=live}}</ref> The country singer [[Jake Owen]] was originally approached to co-write and record the first remix of "Old Town Road".<ref name="JakeOwen">{{Cite web|url=https://bobbybones.iheart.com/featured/bobby-bones/content/2019-05-30-listen-the-unreleased-version-of-old-town-road-with-jake-owen/|last=Huelsman|first=Morgan|title=LISTEN: The Unreleased Version Of "Old Town Road" With Jake Owen|date=May 30, 2019|access-date=August 19, 2019|work=The Bobby Bones Show|publisher=Premiere Networks Inc.|archive-date=August 19, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819200429/https://bobbybones.iheart.com/featured/bobby-bones/content/2019-05-30-listen-the-unreleased-version-of-old-town-road-with-jake-owen/|url-status=live}}</ref> The Columbia Records executive, [[Ron Perry (music)|Ron Perry]], reached out to Cyrus' wife [[Tish Cyrus]] saying that he would love it if Cyrus were to hear "Old Town Road". Cyrus first heard the song over coffee on March 16, 2019, when Tish played it to him.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptKqFafZgCk|title=How Lil Nas X Took 'Old Town Road' From TikTok Meme to No. 1 – Diary of a Song|website=YouTube|publisher=The New York Times|date=May 9, 2019|access-date=July 31, 2019|archive-date=November 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191110153141/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptKqFafZgCk|url-status=live}}</ref> Cyrus explained that he loved the original song the first time he heard it.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/old-town-road-black-cowboys-dom-flemons-818220/|title= 'Old Town Road' and the History of Black Cowboys in America|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=April 5, 2019|access-date=April 5, 2019|author=Jonathan Bernstein|quote=Today, Lil Nas X released a remix of the song with country-crossover singer Billy Ray Cyrus, who says he "loved the song the first time I heard it."}}</ref> Cyrus also mentioned that he related to the song the first time he heard it, connecting the "old town road" to the Old Town Bridge in [[Argillite, Kentucky]], that he used to play on as a child.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1114249608526356480|user=billyraycyrus|title=Congrats @lilnasx 🤠 I'm always in your corner! #1 #OTR #OldTownRoadREMIX<!-- full text of the tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=April 5, 2019|date=April 5, 2019}}</ref> In response to ''Billboard'' removing "Old Town Road" from the Hot Country Songs chart, Cyrus tweeted his support for Lil Nas X and noted that the removal put him in the ranks of great outlaws.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/2019/04/billy-ray-cyrus-lil-nas-x-old-town-road-remix-country.html|title=Billy Ray Cyrus Gives Lil Nas X's 'Old Town Road' a Ringing Endorsement With Remix|author=Dee Locket|website=Vulture|date=April 5, 2019|access-date=April 5, 2019|archive-date=April 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190405211909/https://www.vulture.com/2019/04/billy-ray-cyrus-lil-nas-x-old-town-road-remix-country.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Country rap, and its subgenre, country trap, emerged onto the mainstream following the American rapper Young Thug's experimental mixtape Beautiful Thugger Girls (2017). Lil Nas X has cited Young Thug as a pioneer of country trap. In May 2018, Lil Tracy and Lil Uzi Vert ignited the trend with their country rap single "Like a Farmer (Remix)".

In 2018, Lil Nas X dropped out of college to pursue a music career even though he was discouraged by his parents. He moved in with his sister, spending time promoting his music on the Internet while having just three hours of sleep each night. Lil Nas X found the beat for "Old Town Road" in October 2018 and began writing after his sister told him he had to move out soon. Lil Nas X felt like he was "out of options" and said that his sister's and parents' frustrations with him inspired the song's chorus, "can't nobody tell me nothing". Within a month of writing it, Lil Nas X chose to alter the song's meaning so that the "old town road" would be a symbol of success. Lil Nas X recorded the song on December 2, 2018, at the CinCoYo Recording Studio in Atlanta, and released it the same day on SoundCloud under the title "Old Town Road (I Got the Horses in the Back)".

The Dutch record producer YoungKio produced the beat a year before the song's release and uploaded it as Future Type Beat to his online store for selling beats. He sampled Nine Inch Nails' track "34 Ghosts IV" after finding it from his YouTube algorithm's suggested videos. YoungKio downloaded the song and imported the file to FL Studio, chopping up the Nine Inch Nails sample and filtering it so that it sounded like an old field recording, then reordering sections in an effort to make the austere original more catchy and adding drums underneath. He had never heard of Nine Inch Nails before stumbling upon "34 Ghosts IV". YoungKio did not have the intention of the beat being country related and did not see it as a country music instrumental. Lil Nas X bought the beat from YoungKio for $30, but since purchases on his online store were anonymous, YoungKio did not know the song was purchased by Lil Nas X until he saw it in an Instagram meme in December 2018. Nine Inch Nails founder Trent Reznor later said that, shortly after the song began gaining traction, he received a call from Lil Nas X's manager about the sample, asking for clearance to use it, which he granted. He described the song as "undeniably hooky".

On December 4, 2018, a day after the original version's release, Lil Nas X tweeted that he wanted Billy Ray Cyrus on the song. Lil Nas X knew of Cyrus because of his role on the Disney Channel television series Hannah Montana. The country singer Jake Owen was originally approached to co-write and record the first remix of "Old Town Road". The Columbia Records executive, Ron Perry, reached out to Cyrus' wife Tish Cyrus saying that he would love it if Cyrus were to hear "Old Town Road". Cyrus first heard the song over coffee on March 16, 2019, when Tish played it to him. Cyrus explained that he loved the original song the first time he heard it. Cyrus also mentioned that he related to the song the first time he heard it, connecting the "old town road" to the Old Town Bridge in Argillite, Kentucky, that he used to play on as a child. In response to Billboard removing "Old Town Road" from the Hot Country Songs chart, Cyrus tweeted his support for Lil Nas X and noted that the removal put him in the ranks of great outlaws.

The song is composed in the key of G{{sharp}} minor with a chord progression of G{{sharp}}m-B<sup>add9</sup>-F{{sharp}}-C{{sharp}}m7. It has an approximate tempo of 68 beats per minute.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.text:
thumb|300x300px|Assisted by a remix featuring [[Billy Ray Cyrus (pictured), "Old Town Road" charted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 for a record-setting nineteen weeks.]]
In the United States, the original version of "Old Town Road" reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in the week ending April 13, 2019; at one minute and 53 seconds in length, it became the shortest number-one single since "I'm Henry VIII, I Am" by Herman's Hermits in 1965 and the fifth-shortest in the history of the chart. In the following week, it and the newly released remix featuring Billy Ray Cyrus received a combined 143 million streams, surpassing Drake's "In My Feelings", which in the previous year had amassed 116.2 million in the same period, as the song with the highest single-week streaming figure in the country. This song also became Cyrus's biggest hit in the U.S. since "Achy Breaky Heart" peaked at number four on the Billboard Hot 100 27 years prior. "Old Town Road" continued to exceed 100 million streams in each of the eight following weeks, and in June 2019, was responsible for the three highest weekly U.S. streaming totals in the history of digital music, as well as nine of the eleven highest overall. In October 2019, "Old Town Road" became the fastest single in RIAA history to receive diamond certification in the United States. The certification, which is awarded to singles that attain national combined sales and streams of ten million units, was achieved by the song in its eleventh month of release. The single had sold 1.6 million digital copies in the United States by February 2020.

"Old Town Road" topped the Hot 100 for 19 consecutive weeks from April 13 to August 17, 2019. On August 24, it was finally unseated by Billie Eilish's "Bad Guy" which had waited in the runner-up spot for nine nonconsecutive weeks. "Old Town Road" holds the record for the most consecutive weeks at number one on the Hot 100 chart, surpassing the previous record of 16 weeks achieved by both "One Sweet Day" by Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men (1995–96), and "Despacito" by Luis Fonsi and Daddy Yankee featuring Justin Bieber (2017). Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" broke its record for longest-running number one song (which it held with Shaboozey's "A Bar Song (Tipsy)", which tied its record with 19 non-consecutive weeks at number one in November 2024) in December 2025, achieving 20 non-consecutive weeks at number one on the chart dated December 20, 2025 ("Christmas" has since achieved 22 non-consecutive weeks at number one as of the chart dated January 3, 2026). In July 2019, "Old Town Road" also became the first number-one single on the Rolling Stone Top 100 chart when it held the position in the chart's inaugural edition. In accordance with their methodologies, Billboard and Rolling Stone each assign a single position to "Old Town Road" on their respective charts by combining the performance figures of every released version of the song determined to be sufficiently similar to the original. The former publication credits the entirety of the song's chart run solely to the remix featuring Cyrus.

Elsewhere, the original version of the song topped the national singles charts in at least ten other countries — Australia (thirteen weeks), France and Norway (eight weeks each), Austria (six weeks); Switzerland (five weeks), Denmark, Germany and Ireland (four weeks each), Portugal (three weeks), and the United Kingdom (two weeks) — and charted within the top ten in more than five others. The remix featuring Cyrus achieved a record 19-weeks run at number one on the Canadian Hot 100,{{better source needed|date=November 2019}} and peaked within the top five in more than five other markets.

sections.text: Fellow American country singer Jake Owen and fellow American rapper Lil Wayne both recorded verses for planned remixes that were unofficially released. Owen's remix was shared on The Bobby Bones Show in May 2019 and his verse was later replaced by Ramsey. Lil Wayne's remix was leaked on July 25, 2019, and he performed it live at Lollapalooza the next month. The American rapper Cupcakke released her leaked remix of "Old Town Road", titled "Old Town Hoe", on April 17, 2019. The remix reinterprets the lyric "I'm gonna ride 'til I can't no more" in a sexually explicit way. A music video was released in May 2019 and has Cupcakke and her backup dancers riding toy horses and handling phallic objects, including lollipops, water bottles and corn on the cob. Lil Nas X responded favorably to the remix.

[[Miche Braden]] sang the lead vocals.Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/c0i3TwIHMmg Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20190624192159/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c0i3TwIHMmg&gl=US&hl=en Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite web |date=June 14, 2019 |title=Old Town Road Sung By Blues Legend Miche Braden (LiL Nas X Billy Ray Cover) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c0i3TwIHMmg |website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}} The song was featured in an episode of ''[[The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder]]'', titled "Old Towne Road", with Lil Nas X guest starring as one of the voices. Rather than Billy Ray Cyrus' section of the song, the character of Bobby Proud, voiced by [[Cedric the Entertainer]], joins in with newly written lyrics.{{cite magazine |last=Paul |first=Larisha |date=April 19, 2022 |title=Lil Nas X Returns to His Country Roots With 'Old Town Road' Performance on 'The Proud Family' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lil-nas-x-the-proud-family-louder-and-prouder-1339642/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |magazine=Rolling Stone}} The song was included in [["Weird Al" Yankovic]]'s 2024 polka medley "[[List of "Weird Al" Yankovic polka medleys#"Polkamania!"|Polkamania!]]".
sections.text: The actor-comedian Omi Vaidya parodied the song with "Oak Tree Road", a song about Asian Indian culture in the US. Postmodern Jukebox also covered the song, doing it in the style of a New Orleans blues song. Miche Braden sang the lead vocals. The song was featured in an episode of The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder, titled "Old Towne Road", with Lil Nas X guest starring as one of the voices. Rather than Billy Ray Cyrus' section of the song, the character of Bobby Proud, voiced by Cedric the Entertainer, joins in with newly written lyrics. The song was included in "Weird Al" Yankovic's 2024 polka medley "Polkamania!".
